scientific_scope.statement: not_conjecture1 : not Conjecture1, where Conjecture1 says: for every n and every simple graph G on Fin n with no non-trivial module, (every blowup of G by non-empty cliques is recolorable) iff (every induced subgraph of G is recolorable); recolorable means R_l connected for every l >= chi + 1. Instance theorem 'witness': C9 is prime, all 512 induced subgraphs of C9 are recolorable, and the blowup of C9 with every vertex replaced by K2 is not recolorable (chi = 5, the period-three six-colouring is an isolated vertex of R_6 and a second proper six-colouring exists). Variant not_conjecture1Connected adds the hypothesis that G is connected.
binding_points: infinite range of l in the antecedent closed by a general degeneracy lemma (mix_rel, recolorable_induce), not by computation
chi(C9[S]) >= d(S)+1 for every non-empty S (c9_chi), so l >= chi+1 implies l >= d+2; empty S handled separately
relative colourings (ProperOn/Reach on the ambient vertex set) transferred to the literal reconfiguration graph of the induced subgraph on the subtype (reach_to_path)
chi(H) = 5 exactly (H_isChi5), so l = 6 is chi+1
R_6(H) disconnected: no Path from the frozen colouring to a second proper colouring (H_not_mixing6), not merely existence of a frozen colouring
G connected (source's standing assumption): c9_connected, not_conjecture1Connected
H equals the archived 18-vertex graph of the checker and of ../../c9_kernel (H_adj_archived)
scientific_scope.not_claimed: the converse direction; the C_n[K_2] family and the 90*2^n count; that the version of record words the conjecture identically; novelty beyond the qualification in PRIOR_WORK.md
scope_sentences_to_carry_with_FULL: Only the direction 'every induced subgraph of G recolorable implies every blowup of G recolorable' is refuted; the converse is untouched.

FULL is relative to the arXiv v2 wording of Conjecture 1 (identical in v1); the version of record (J. Graph Theory 111(4) (2026) 113-123) was not readable (HTTP 403) and has been read by nobody in this project.
